claim: In a simulation-based-calibration test using real precinct/voter-file covariates from the 2018 MA-7 Democratic primary but a known synthetic vote-choice model, precinct-aggregated ecological inference (EI) point estimates (z-scores) performed as well as, or slightly better than, individual-level inference that has access to (simulated) individual vote choice directly.
stance_target: EI point-estimate accuracy necessarily degrades relative to individual-level baselines at fine geography
scope_conditions: simulation study, 2018 MA-7 Democratic primary voter file, correctly-specified linear model, single election
quoted_support: In fact, a closer look at the z-scores suggests that the EI point estimate performed better on average than individual inference... this is also acting as a sort of noise filter, reducing the chances that model infers an incorrect value.

claim: Despite point estimates holding up well under aggregation to precinct level, the EI method's posterior uncertainty was overdispersed relative to individual-level inference (S-shaped rank-statistic distribution vs near-uniform), meaning EI confidence intervals are less well-calibrated/less identified even when point accuracy does not suffer.
stance_target: point-estimate accuracy and CI calibration can diverge -- point estimates can survive aggregation to fine geography even as calibration degrades
quoted_support: For the conventional individual level inference we get pretty close to uniformity, but for ecological inference we see an S-shaped distribution. This indicates that the posterior computed with EI is overdispersed, meaning it is more uncertain than it should be.

claim: The authors caveat that their favorable EI point-accuracy result is from a single election with a correctly-specified data-generating model, and that identification difficulty for EI depends on how well-sorted voters are by salient characteristics, so results may not generalize across elections.
stance_target: generalizability of favorable EI accuracy findings
quoted_support: This experiment was encouraging, although fairly limited in scope. There is no guarantee that these results will generalize because the difficulties in identification for EI will depend on how well-sorted voters are by salient characteristics, making every election unique.
